title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZD (Transferability of shares and attendant rights)

content.overview: Section 378ZD generally restricts transfer of a Member's shares in a Producer Company, subject to statutory exceptions. A Member may transfer all or part of shares with any special rights to an active Member at par value after prior Board approval. Members must nominate a person within three months of membership for vesting on death. The section addresses nominee rights and surrender where the nominee is not a producer, and requires written notice and an opportunity to be heard before the Board directs surrender because a Member ceased to be a primary producer or lost membership qualifications under the articles.
content.glance: Section 378ZD restricts share transfers, allows an approved transfer to an active Member at par, requires nomination within three months, and sets death and qualification-loss rules with safeguards.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZD (Transferability of shares and attendant rights). Except as provided in subsections (2) to (4), a Member's shares in a Producer Company are not transferable. A Member may, with prior Board approval, transfer all or part of shares and any special rights to an active Member at par value. Each Member must nominate a person in the manner specified in the articles within three months of becoming a Member for the shares to vest on death. On death, the nominee becomes entitled to the rights in the shares and the Board transfers them to the nominee; if the nominee is not a producer, the Board directs surrender of the shares and any special rights to the company at par value or another value determined by the Board. If the Board is satisfied that a Member ceased to be a primary producer or failed to retain qualifications specified in the articles, it must direct surrender on the stated valuation basis, but only after written notice and an opportunity to be heard. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: General restriction and approved transfer
sections.body: Except as otherwise provided in subsections (2) to (4), a Member's shares in a Producer Company are not transferable. A Member may, after obtaining prior Board approval, transfer all or part of the shares along with any special rights to an active Member at par value.

sections.heading: Nomination within three months
sections.body: Every Member must, within three months of becoming a Member, nominate in the manner specified in the articles a person to whom the shares shall vest on the Member's death.

sections.heading: Rights of nominee on death
sections.body: On the Member's death, the nominee becomes entitled to all rights in the shares and the Board transfers the deceased Member's shares to the nominee. If the nominee is not a producer, the Board must direct surrender of the shares and any special rights to the Producer Company at par value or another value determined by the Board.

sections.heading: Surrender after loss of qualification
sections.body: Where the Board is satisfied that a Member has ceased to be a primary producer or has failed to retain qualifications for membership specified in the articles, it must direct surrender of the shares and any special rights to the Producer Company at par value or another value determined by the Board. It may not direct surrender unless the Member has received written notice and an opportunity to be heard.

examples.title: Assessing a proposed share transfer
examples.body: Check whether the transferee is an active Member, whether prior Board approval was obtained, and whether the transfer is at par value. For death or loss of qualification, apply the separate nomination or surrender provisions and their safeguards.

hypotheticals.question: The Board proposes to require a Member to surrender shares after concluding that the Member is no longer a primary producer. What must be checked under section 378ZD?
hypotheticals.analysis: Confirm the Board's satisfaction on the statutory ground, check the membership qualifications specified in the articles, and verify that written notice and an opportunity to be heard were provided before the Board directs surrender. Do not treat a loss-of-qualification decision as removing the express procedural safeguard.

misconceptions.trap: Treating Member shares as freely transferable.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (1) states the general restriction, subject to the specified statutory exceptions.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a transfer to any person is permitted after Board approval.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (2) identifies an active Member as transferee and requires transfer at par value.

misconceptions.trap: Directing surrender for loss of qualification without notice and an opportunity to be heard.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (5) expressly requires written notice and an opportunity to be heard before such surrender.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zd do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Save as the section provides, the shares of a Member of a Producer Company are not transferable. A transfer of the whole or part to an active Member at par value needs previous Board approval.
